title: Compute ferromagnetic spinodal temperature T_ms
action: Solve the saddle-point equation for the effective field h as a function of temperature for connectivity k=3. Identify T_ms as the highest temperature where a nonzero solution h exists. Write the value to T_ms.txt.
description: The ferromagnetic spinodal temperature T_ms, above which no nonzero solution for the effective field h exists.
output_schema: Single float value on one line.

title: Compute first-order ferromagnetic transition temperature T_fm
action: Using the ferromagnetic free-energy expression and the paramagnetic free-energy expression for k=3, find the temperature T_fm below T_ms at which the ferromagnetic free energy becomes lower than the paramagnetic one. Write the value to T_fm.txt.
description: The first-order ferromagnetic transition temperature T_fm, where the ferromagnetic free energy becomes thermodynamically dominant.
output_schema: Single float value on one line.

title: Determine glass transition temperatures T_c and T_K from 1-RSB variational approximation
action: Implement the 1-RSB variational free energy for k=3 with parameters Δ and m. Optimize free energy across a range of temperatures to locate: (i) T_c where a nontrivial solution first appears with m=1, and (ii) T_K where m becomes less than 1 and the glassy free energy becomes lower than the paramagnetic one. Write both values to T_c_and_T_K.txt in the format 'T_c <value> T_K <value>'.
description: The dynamical glass transition temperature T_c and the Kauzmann temperature T_K from the 1-RSB variational approximation.

title: Compute configurational entropy at T_c
action: From the variational 1-RSB free energy, compute the configurational entropy at T_c as the free-energy difference between the glassy and paramagnetic states. Write the value to S_conf_at_Tc.txt.
description: The configurational entropy at the dynamical glass transition temperature T_c from the 1-RSB variational approximation.
output_schema: Single float value on one line.
